data.long_meaning: In Hindu mythology, Nalakanta refers to Lord Shiva who wears the serpent Vasuki around his neck. The name Nalakanta carries the meaning “Lord of the serpent” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit, Hindi, etc. tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Nalakanta usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of the serpent and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Nalakanta total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Nalakanta" is deeply rooted in Hindu mythology, specifically relating to the incarnation of Lord Shiva who holds the king cobra Vasuki around his neck. This serpent had been used as a weapon by other gods to churn the cosmic ocean, and after the task was complete, Lord Shiva graciously took the serpent as a symbol of his control over the universe's primal forces (like creation, destruction, and transformation). In Hindu art, Nalakanta is depicted as a powerful deity with Vasuki, and this image can be found in many temples and religious sites across India.
data.spiritual_significance: The Hindu name "Nalakanta" carries deep spiritual significance, reminding us of Lord Shiva's mastery over the cosmic forces, his protective qualities, and the importance of embracing and harnessing the primal energies within us. This name inspires an ongoing quest for spiritual growth, inner transformation, and self-realization. Nalakanta serves as a reminder that, like Lord Shiva, we too can find balance and harmony in the cycles of life and overcome all challenges by acknowledging and embracing the powerful energies within.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Nalakanta symbolizes the triumph over inner demons. The name is derived from the words 'Nala' (inner self) and 'Kanta' (vanquisher). It signifies the victorious quest for self-realization and purification.

vedic_reference.note: Nal means 'lotus stalk' or 'garland' and Kanta means 'wearer' or 'lord'.

historical_references.reference: Nalakanta was an epithet used for the god Shiva during the Chola period. Shiva was considered the presiding deity of the Chola dynasty and was often invoked for protection and prosperity.
Nalakanta was also an epithet used for the god Vishnu during the medieval period in Kerala. Vishnu was regarded as the protector of the Kerala Kings and was invoked for their victory and prosperity.

modern_usage.modern_context: In Hindu mythology, Nalakanta is a revered name associated with Lord Vishnu. It is believed that Lord Vishnu appeared in the form of Nalakanta to destroy the demon king, Vali. Today, Nalakanta is seen in various modern contexts across multiple platforms. In Books and Literature, several works have been dedicated to the legend of Nalakanta, providing a deeper understanding of the story and its significance. In Television and Media, Nalakanta's story has been portrayed in various series and documentaries, offering visual representations and interpretations of the myth. In Gaming and Entertainment, Nalakanta's tale has been adapted into video games, allowing players to experience the legend in an interactive and immersive way.
